trust_decision.summary: Group-level read RBAC on a public org/project/asset marks a non-member request as IsPublicRequest and lets it continue; each write route must then itself reject public requests (DisallowPublicRequests) or require write RBAC (assetScopedRBAC ActionUpdate), decided per route in the router/ registration files.

landing_point.why: 'improper authorization on public assets' points at AssetAccessControlFactory, where asset.IsPublic && ActionRead sets IsPublicRequest and passes; the real fix is per-route in router/*.go, not here.

fix_sites.entry_point: new DisallowPublicRequests middleware (fix.diff:13-21), used by the routes below
none (fix only adds a blank line, fix.diff:60)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All sites are sibling route registrations in router/ (one package) plus the one new middleware; no second implementation, lower-level API or serialization path is involved.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the O8 GET route: 'it is a GET, the protection is about write methods (the fix's own regression test skips every GET), and it is a GitHub App installation callback rather than an asset write route.'

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Read-only org members (RoleMember gets only ActionRead) must keep triaging vulns, license risks and VEX rules; the fix deliberately uses DisallowPublicRequests, not ActionUpdate RBAC, on those routes. A blanket 'require assetScopedRBAC ActionUpdate on every write' breaks member triage. Separately, public read GETs on the same groups must keep working for non-members.

O6_input_shapes: HTTP methods POST, PUT, DELETE on asset-version subroutes
two protection kinds: write RBAC (artifact/external-reference/artifact-create) vs public-only block (triage routes)
public flag set at org (MultiOrganizationMiddlewareRBAC / OrganizationAccessControlMiddleware), project or asset level

O7_producer.where: IsPublicRequest state is set by middleware in the same request (middlewares/access_control_middlewares.go:133); no schema/serializer/cache producer.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET org-scoped /integrations/finish-installation/ binds a GitHub App installation to the org (DB write) behind only org read RBAC, so a non-member of a public org passes as IsPublicRequest.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a GET and an installation callback; the published fix and its test only cover non-GET routes.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET org-scoped /trigger-sync/ runs an external-entity project refresh behind only org read RBAC, reachable by a public-org non-member.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: GET, only does anything for external-entity orgs, and it syncs with the caller's own identity (services/external_entity_provider_service.go:51-62), so it plausibly writes nothing the visitor can see.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a POST /crowdsourced-vexing/apply/ registered with only NeededScope(manage)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: this sub-router takes no repository and has no RBAC factory, matching the pattern of the vulnerable routers before the fix.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a project-level release write route on projectRouter instead of projectUpdateAccessControlRequired
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: releases already mix read routes on projectRouter with writes on the update group; a maintainer could register one on the wrong group. Different layer (project RBAC), so this is a how-type extra.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a DELETE /events/ bulk route or a POST under /events/ without EventMiddleware/assetScopedRBAC
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the single-event delete at line 75 already chains three middlewares by hand, so an omitted one is a typical copy slip.

O9_family: missing authorization on write routes under public-read RBAC (CWE-285/863, per-route middleware omission)

services: PostgreSQL for the full server and integration tests (testcontainers, go.mod:54-55); not needed for router-level tests that use mocks/
O10_build.project_tests: router/oci_registry_router_test.go exists at the pinned commit; the fix adds router/router_test.go, which builds the real router tree with mocks/ and walks e.Routes() (fix.diff:293-585). Hidden tests in that style run offline.

j.j_sites_touched: middlewares/access_control_middlewares.go, router/artifact_router.go, router/asset_router.go, router/asset_version_router.go, router/dependency_vuln_router.go, router/external_reference_router.go, router/first_party_vuln_router.go, router/license_risk_router.go, router/vex_rule_router.go
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Change AssetAccessControlFactory/ProjectAccessControlFactory so public read is granted only for GET, or add assetScopedRBAC(ActionUpdate) to every write route. The first misses the org-level public path and breaks nothing obvious; the second locks read-only members out of vuln triage.

out_of_scope_notes: router/dependency_proxy_router.go:25 POST /npm/* and router/apiv1_router.go:269-270 are unauthenticated by design and outside the org-scoped RBAC chain; not pursued.
Whether triage controllers check that :dependencyVulnID/:ruleId belong to the routed asset version (IDOR) was not checked.
unverified: present_in_latest for both O8 routes: no latest release given.
Whether a public visitor can supply a valid unbound installationId for finish-installation in practice (needs a row in github_app_installations) was not traced.
O1 counts the 21 route registrations whose middleware the fix changed (2 artifact, 2 asset-version, 4 dependency-vuln, 2 first-party, 4 license-risk, 4 VEX-rule, 3 external-reference).

Pattern A fit rests on the wide spread of route sites and the member-only coupled behaviour, not on an out-of-scope-looking module (O2 is none); the routes are all of one concept, which lessons-v2 says tends to get fixed together.
Whether external-entity RBAC (accesscontrol/external_entity_provider_rbac.go:103) changes who counts as a public visitor was not traced.
